clue.text: Accommodation from fourth and fifth of August

explanation.definitionFit: Quarters are lodgings, especially those assigned to soldiers or servants, so they are a form of housing.

clue.text: That chap weighed down by mostly fast food

clue.text: Country where sledging originated?

explanation.walkthrough: Snow and sleds lead to Scandinavia; the cricketing sense points to a hot country instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, sledging means insulting batsmen to break their concentration, a practice and word credited to Australian players.

clue.text: Clear level of electoral engagement

second meaning: the proportion of voters who go to the polls

explanation.definitionFit: Turnout is the share of the electorate that actually votes, and in Britain also a good clear-out of a room.

explanation.walkthrough: Wonga is British slang for money.

clue.text: Objective of one occupying a sunbed at sea

clue.text: Weapon no US TV star will back

clue.text: Nice tax breaks not definite

clue.text: Australian creature having advantage over a tailless species

clue.text: Exercise entails running, that brings disadvantages

clue.text: Shot captain oddly dropped then caught — sensational!

clue.text: Cutting down gin cured shakes
